messages:
mira: Heads-up — customer asked how we separate audit logs between tenants. They want strict isolation so members in tenant A cannot see events from tenant B. Are we currently storing tenant_id in the audit events and enforcing RBAC at query time?

ajohnson: We do include tenant_id in the event schema but enforcement is a mix. Hosted: query layer has a tenant filter for most endpoints. Dedicated/private: it's expected the tenant will host logs or we scope the API key. Not sure about the console UI views though.

samir: Console is a gap — the UI currently filters by org but admins can toggle scopes. We had a TODO to treat audit-read as a scoped permission (admin vs member).

mira: Can we confirm whether scoped tokens (short-lived audience-scoped) are enforced for the audit-read endpoints? Also want to validate that exported customer-facing audit events (CSV/JSON) redact any cross-tenant identifiers.

adam: @mira FYI I filed a quick repro where a scoped token issued with membership role could fetch /v1/audit/events?tenant_id=<other>. It failed locally due to a missing middleware, will open PR.

mira: Thanks. If there’s a middleware gap, it’s a critical bug. This is both a security and compliance risk for SOC2 customers.

samir: Question — do we treat tenant admins vs org admins differently? Some customers have shared admins across multiple tenants. The audit logs must be visible to tenant admins only unless they explicitly enable cross-tenant adminship.

adam: We have an internal flag on the account model: cross_tenant_admins boolean. Default false. If true, RBAC allows admin to query across tenant_ids. But that flag should be gated behind SSO/admin onboarding and recorded in audit logs.

dana: For KMS integration: when we export logs (S3) we encrypt with customer-managed key in Private deployments. Hosted customers rely on our KMS; we rotate keys quarterly. Need to ensure audit events metadata includes KMS key_id used for encryption so customers can validate.

mira: Agreed. Add key_id to exported metadata. Also, which fields are PII and should be redacted by default? We need a small schema subset for customer-facing exports.

samir: Proposed minimal export schema: timestamp, tenant_id (masked if cross-tenant not allowed?), actor_id (hashed), action, resource_type, resource_id (truncated), outcome, request_id, kms_key_id. Sharing a quick snippet:

```json
{"timestamp":"iso8601","tenant_id":"string","actor_id":"sha256","action":"string","resource_type":"string","resource_id":"string_trunc","outcome":"ok|fail","request_id":"uuid","kms_key_id":"arn"}
```

mira: That looks good. For tenant_id masking — better to drop full tenant names and use internal tenant hash to avoid leaking customer names in multi-tenant exports.

adam: PR opened: https://git.internal/repo/redwood-infra/pull/4523 — adds middleware check and test coverage. Failing CI due to integration test around scoped tokens.

mira: Can someone run the vuln triage on the PR? We should treat this as P0 until tests show scoped token enforcement everywhere. Also add a regression test that attempts to query events with a token scoped to a different tenant.

samir: I'll take the triage. Quick notes: 1) Verify token audience claim (aud) matches tenant_id, 2) Ensure console GraphQL resolvers apply tenant scoping, 3) Validate exports pipeline honors masking.

adam: For immediate mitigation, we can disable cross-tenant queries in hosted API gate for the next deploy and add a feature flag to re-enable once fixed.

mira: Good plan. Action items: @adam — fix middleware + add regression test (PR 4523). @samir — run vuln triage and confirm impacted surfaces. @dana — update export schema and ensure kms_key_id is included. I'll draft a short customer-facing note explaining that we found an enforcement gap, it’s patched in next deploy, and exports are safe.

dana: Will update the export schema doc and add tests for encryption metadata.

audit-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-134 — Audit API tenant filter enforcement. Severity: High. Assigned: samir, adam, dana.

mira: Thanks all. Let's sync after Adam's CI green. If triage finds anything else escalate to oncall. :thumbsup:
